version.changelog: BREAKING: --token required for all scripts (env var removed). Fully platform-agnostic, zero environment dependencies. 105 tests. See upgrade guide in SKILL.md.

llm.summary: The skill's code matches its Notion sync purpose, but packaging and runtime instructions contain inconsistencies and an explicit security concern: it requires passing your Notion token on the command line (which can leak credentials) and the registry metadata omits required runtime details.

dimensions.detail: The code files implement the advertised Notion sync capabilities (search, query, md↔Notion, watch, update, delete). However the registry metadata lists no required binaries or primary credential while the SKILL.md and scripts require Node.js v18+ and a Notion integration token. The capabilities themselves match the description, but the metadata is incomplete.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts operate only against api.notion.com and local files, which is expected. However v2.0 requires passing the Notion token via a --token CLI argument (the code no longer reads NOTION_API_KEY). Requiring the secret on the command line is a security concern because process arguments and shell history can leak the token. The scripts also read and write local files (markdown input/output and a state file memory/notion-watch-state.json), which is expected for this tool but should be noted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (no downloads or package installs), which reduces some risks. But the project requires Node.js v18+ to run the included scripts; the registry metadata 'required binaries: none' is inconsistent with that requirement. No external URLs or archive installs are used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The scripts require a Notion integration token, but the skill metadata lists no primary credential or required env vars. The design intentionally takes the token as a CLI argument (not an env var). That is coherent as a design choice but it is not declared in the registry and is less secure than reading a token from a protected environment variable or secret store.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or claim persistent platform privileges. It writes a local state file under the workspace (memory/notion-watch-state.json) and reads/writes markdown files in the current workspace — expected behavior for a sync/monitoring tool and scoped to the workspace rather than system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's code implements a typical Notion sync tool, but before installing or running it consider: 1) Node requirement: you need Node.js v18+ to run the scripts (the registry metadata does not declare this). 2) Token handling: v2 requires you pass the Notion integration token with --token on the command line — this can expose the token via process lists or shell history. Prefer running from a wrapper that injects the token from a protected secret store or use an environment variable if you adapt the scripts. 3) Filesystem effects: the scripts read local markdown files and write a state file at memory/notion-watch-state.json in the current workspace; run in a workspace you trust. 4) Least privilege: create a Notion integration with only the permissions/pages needed and only share the pages/databases the integration requires. 5) Origin and review: the homepage points to a GitHub repo — inspect the code yourself (or run in an isolated environment) before giving it your tokens. If you want to proceed, avoid passing tokens directly on the shell command line or modify the scripts to read the token from a secure environment variable or secret manager.
